sentence_stem: Had the committee been informed earlier,
correct_completion: the proposal would have been approved.
full_sentence: Had the committee been informed earlier, the proposal would have been approved.
acceptable_variants: the outcome would almost certainly have been favourable.
the proposal might well have passed.

options.text: the proposal will be reviewed next week.
options.why_wrong: A simple future does not match the hypothetical past condition set by the inverted 'Had' clause.

options.text: the proposal had been approved already.
options.why_wrong: A past perfect describes an earlier fact, not the hypothetical outcome of a condition that was never met.

options.text: the proposal would have been approved.

options.why_wrong: This is ungrammatical as a main clause. A participial phrase cannot complete the sentence on its own.

grammar_focus: Third conditional with inverted 'had' in formal written English
explanation: The inverted 'Had + subject + past participle' structure replaces 'If the committee had been informed'. The main clause therefore needs 'would have' plus a past participle to express a hypothetical result in the past.
translation: Se o comitê tivesse sido informado antes, a proposta teria sido aprovada.
